sections.what: Runs unit tests in a Node environment from the tests/unit folder, with one database setup step, one file at a time, long time limits and a coverage report. The engine, rights, llm and chart folders are measured, and the engine folder must reach 100 percent.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the strict engine gate; likely because it is the core logic.
sections.watch_out: Only the engine folder is gated, so coverage in the llm and rights folders can drop without failing the run.

summary: Unit test settings: where the tests are, the test environment, a one-time database setup step, and a 100 percent coverage gate on the engine folder.
purpose: Run quick logic tests and enforce full coverage on the core engine.
why: Likely reason for the strict engine gate: the core logic is pure and should be fully tested. Likely reason for running one file at a time: the tests share one database.
how: 1) The test runner loads the at sign alias. 2) It runs the one-time database setup. 3) It runs each test file in turn. 4) It measures coverage for four folders and fails the run if the engine folder is below 100 percent.
inputs: Test files under tests/unit and the source files they cover.
outputs: Test results and a coverage summary.
risks: Only the engine folder has the 100 percent gate, so the other measured folders can lose coverage unnoticed. Running files one at a time is slower.
debug: If the run fails with a coverage message, look at the uncovered engine lines. If tests cannot reach the database, check the setup file. If imports fail, check the at sign alias.
